title: Difference between a Convex and  Concave Polygon
description:
Polygons come in all kinds of shapes and sizes. In this video I cover the difference between a convex polygon and a concave polygon.

One key difference is that a convex polygon has all interior angles less than 180° and no inward vertices, while a concave polygon has at least one angle greater than 180° and at least one vertex that points inward.

asr.full_text: How is a convex polygon different than a concave polygon? First, With a convex polygon all interior angles are 180 degrees or less. With a concave polygon, one of more or less of the interior angles are greater than 180 degrees. If you draw a line through a convex polygon, it will only strike or intersect at two places. If you draw a line through a concave polygon, it will intersect the polygon in more than two places. With a convex polygon it has the appearance as if all the vertices are pointed outward. With a concave polygon it looks like one vertex has been pushed inward. It looks like a cave, which is a good way to remember the difference between each two. Thanks for watching and remember kindness multiplies kindness. Be kind to someone today.
